parts.name: body shell

physics.Basic_description: Orange rectangular block with a matte plastic finish, housing the locking mechanism and keyway.
physics.Functional_description: Encases the internal locking pins and provides the main structural body for the lock.
physics.Grasped_description: A parallel jaw gripper can firmly grasp the sides of the orange body to stabilize or move the lock.
physics.reason: Molded plastic lock bodies are thin-walled shells enclosing air and internal metal components, not solid blocks of plastic.

parts.description: Orange rectangular block with a matte plastic finish, housing the locking mechanism and keyway.
parts.function: Encases the internal locking pins and provides the main structural body for the lock.

parts.name: keyway disc

physics.Basic_description: Small circular silver metallic disc centered on the front face of the orange body.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a wear-resistant interface for the key and guides it into the locking mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be grasped effectively; serves as a visual landmark only.
physics.reason: Keyway discs are typically solid stamped or machined metal plates.

parts.description: Small circular silver metallic disc centered on the front face of the orange body.
parts.function: Provides a wear-resistant interface for the key and guides it into the locking mechanism.

parts.name: keyway slot

physics.Basic_description: Tiny dark vertical slot in the center of the keyway disc.
physics.Functional_description: The physical aperture where the key blade is inserted to actuate the lock.
physics.Grasped_description: Not graspable; it is a negative space feature for key insertion.
physics.reason: Modeled as the solid material boundary of the slot or the internal plug surface.

parts.description: Tiny dark vertical slot in the center of the keyway disc.
parts.function: The physical aperture where the key blade is inserted to actuate the lock.

parts.name: shackle bar

physics.Basic_description: White U-shaped metal bar with a smooth, possibly coated or galvanized finish, extending from the body.
physics.Functional_description: The locking loop that passes through the hasp or chain to secure the equipment.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by the top arch or side legs, though the body is preferred for stability.
physics.reason: Shackles are solid metal rods designed to resist cutting and pulling forces.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
